title: M5GFX #442 review: keep M5IOE1 GPIO1 low for StopWatch Type-C USB

hardware.target: M5Stack StopWatch C152 (ESP32-S3R8, M5PM1, M5IOE1, CH442E, CO5300 466x466)

firmware.build: ESP-IDF v6.1, target esp32s3, 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM; M5GFX as IDF component at PR head / develop tip; probe app calls M5GFX::init() then reads M5IOE1 0x03/0x05/0x13 over port 1 (SDA 47, SCL 48)

execution.environment: macOS arm64 read-only source review; local ESP-IDF v6.1 build for ESP32-S3; local Device Service stopwatch profile (QEMU m5stopwatch, CO5300 466x466, M5PM1 + M5IOE1 modelled); host board_detect tests

checks.detail: PR #442 OPEN, not draft, author hlym123, English title and body, 0 comments and 0 reviews before review, mergeable MERGEABLE, head cc6d5ff, base 92bd25c (= develop tip), 3 files +45/-5

0x03/0x05/0x13 are GPIO_M_L/GPIO_O_L/GPIO_DRV_L with O1/M1/DRV1 as bit 0 (datasheet p.6; M5Unified M5IOE1_Class constants); gpio1 = 0 and _bitForPin/_regForPin make GPIO1 bit 0; PYG1 is PYB_MUX_CTR to CH442E IN, so clearing 0x05 bit0 and dropping 0x01 from 0x99 targets the intended pin

the latch is written low before 0x13 (push-pull) and 0x03 (output enable), which is the correct order for a retained high latch; fixture s3.txt:187 and the new ops_host.cpp case encode the same order (6:1,5,0,1 before 6:1,19,0,157)

git grep at head: pmic_ops.hpp is the only M5IOE1 writer in M5GFX and there is no other MUX_CTR reference; M5Unified's M5IOE1_Class::gpio1 writes belong to CoreMatrix (TF power) and CoreP4X (audio power), not StopWatch
M5StopWatch-UserDemo main/hal/hal_ioe.cpp:32 labels M5IOE1_PIN_1 as CH442E MUX CONTROL and :76 writes 0, so the new low default matches M5Stack's own application firmware

stopwatch profile: PR build reports IOE1 mode=0x9D out=0x98 drv=0x00 (GPIO1=0) and stays 0x98 over three 1 s samples; develop build reports out=0x99 (GPIO1=1); both identify board_M5StopWatch and render a 468x468 frame

0x03=0x9D and 0x13=0x00 in both builds, i.e. GPIO3/4/5/8 still outputs with push-pull; the 10 ms/8 ms TP_RST+OLED_RST pulse and L3B_EN are unchanged; first frame renders and the probe text is drawn on the panel
sh test/board_detect/run.sh at PR head: C++ test programs: 34 passed, including the new test_stopwatch_typec_usb_default

public C152 schematic VA_20251201 page 4 places CH442E commons on MUX_IO_1/2 (rear header) with the note 'PYB_MUX_CTR selects U0TXD/U0RXD when low, and USB_P/USB_N when high', and Type-C is wired straight to USB_P/N on page 3; on that revision a high G1 adds the rear header in parallel rather than disconnecting Type-C, so the V1.1 rewiring cited in the commit message needs a schematic/ECO reference

after the change nothing in M5GFX/M5Unified drives GPIO1 high during board init, so the rear J5/J6 header defaults to UART0 instead of USB; an application can still drive it through M5.getIOExpander(0), but the previous board-level default is gone and is not mentioned in the commit message
no physical StopWatch with an observable Type-C data path on this host; actual USB enumeration on Type-C and on the rear header was not exercised

the warm variant forced GPIO1 high and called esp_restart(); the virtual guest printed rst:0xc (RTC_SW_CPU_RST) and then stopped before the second-stage bootloader, so the pre-init window could not be observed; this is an emulator limitation, not a PR finding
the stopwatch virtual device models M5PM1/M5IOE1 registers but no USB PHY or CH442E routing, so only the IOE1 register state is observable; link-level behaviour on either connector is not

notes: PR left OPEN; exactly one English comment posted; no close, no push, no change to m5stack/M5GFX.
Build used local copies of both trees; the only build-system edit was adding esp_psram to the IDF>=6 requires of CMakeLists.txt in those copies (no src/ change).
Evidence class is virtual-device validation for the register effect plus code-level verification; hardware validation and the warm-restart path are NOT RUN.
